tier_reason: http-arena.com/data.json results unary-grpc-256/1024 list wtx (3,990,708 / 3,620,970 rps) and grpc-go (720,798 / 969,718 rps) on the same board; benchmark code is public in MDA2AV/HttpArena (frameworks/wtx-grpc, frameworks/grpc-go, h2load harness), with toolchains and flags in the Dockerfiles/Cargo.toml and the CPU model (Threadripper PRO 3995WX) stated in the hardware docs and data.json.

corrections.compiler_and_flags: wtx: Rust nightly-2026-06-27 (rust:1.95 base image), `RUSTFLAGS="-C target-cpu=native" cargo build --release` with release profile opt-level=3, lto="thin", codegen-units=1, panic="abort"; wtx 0.49 (features grpc-server, optimizations-std, quick-protobuf, tokio) per frameworks/wtx-grpc/Dockerfile and Cargo.toml in MDA2AV/HttpArena. grpc-go: Go 1.24 (golang:1.24-bookworm image), `CGO_ENABLED=0 go build`, google.golang.org/grpc v1.72.0, default grpc.NewServer() with GOMAXPROCS=NumCPU (frameworks/grpc-go).
corrections.hardware: AMD Ryzen Threadripper PRO 3995WX (Zen 2, 64 cores / 128 threads, single NUMA node, performance governor). Per HttpArena's Hardware & Topology docs, the server is pinned to a 64-thread cpuset (0-31,64-95 = 32 physical cores plus SMT siblings) and the load generator to the other half of the same chip; every run uses the same machine.
corrections.workload: Unary gRPC GetSum call (9-byte protobuf request) over plaintext HTTP/2 (h2c), h2load load generator with 256 and 1024 connections and 100 concurrent streams per connection, 5s duration, 3 runs with the best taken, on the HttpArena multi-language benchmark harness.
corrections.caveats: wtx's server process used ~64 logical CPUs (6379-6383% cpu) versus grpc-go's ~44 (4339-4478% cpu) during the run, so throughput-per-core is not directly comparable, only end-to-end rps on shared hardware. The two results were not measured in the same session: grpc-go's unary-grpc numbers have been unchanged since an HttpArena results update on 2026-04-12 (commit f326f067), while wtx's current numbers come from a re-run on 2026-08-24 (PR #1300), and the harness evolved in between. wtx's earlier published unary-grpc numbers (2026-07-30 to 2026-08-24) were invalid: its handler returned an empty reply body that h2load did not detect; body validation caught it, the entry was disabled (PR #1291), fixed and re-validated in PR #1300. The figures above are the post-fix validated numbers. The harness (HttpArena, github.com/MDA2AV/HttpArena, MIT-licensed) is a general full-stack web-framework benchmark, not an RPC-specific shootout. The wtx-grpc entry was contributed by wtx's own author (c410-f3r, PRs #812 and #1056), so it is not a fully arms-length third party, although the Dockerfiles, build commands and raw JSON results are public and runs are done centrally by the HttpArena maintainers. grpc-go is labeled 'tuned' but runs a default grpc.NewServer(). tonic (Rust's main gRPC framework) has a directory in the repo and was benchmarked in an April 2026 pre-round (378,723 rps at 256 connections, commit 2b36f907), but it is absent from the current results, so no current same-language comparison exists. wtx is not the fastest entry on the board: zix, cardigan and swerver post about 6.8-7.0M rps in the same test.

notes: Numbers, ratios (5.54x at 256 conns, 3.73x at 1024 conns), and all repository metadata (MPL-2.0, 401 stars, last commit 2026-09-08, not a fork, not archived) are confirmed. The corrections make the hardware description precise (the server gets 32 physical cores plus SMT, not 64 dedicated cores), add the exact toolchains and workload parameters, and add caveats about the different run dates and wtx's earlier invalid, since-fixed result. Tier A stays.
